notes.title: FY27 IT Capital Plan
notes.content:
Kestrel Health — FY27 IT Capital Plan

Total approved: $4.2M
Committed to date: $3.89M
Uncommitted: $310K

Major lines:
- EHR optimisation programme: $1.6M
- Network refresh, Sites 2 and 4: $980K
- Endpoint replacement (1,100 devices): $640K
- Clinical documentation pilot (TechFlow): $180K/yr, not yet committed
- Contingency: $310K

The uncommitted balance is the negotiating margin for Q3 sourcing. Not to be shared outside Finance and Procurement.

notes.title: Vendor Portfolio Review — Q1 FY27
notes.content:
IT Steering Committee, 12 Feb 2027

Clinical documentation category reviewed. Three vendors shortlisted, one advanced to limited pilot.

Advanced: TechFlow AI. Selected on integration depth and time-to-value, not on price. Pilot scope: two medical-surgical units, de-identified data only.

Decision gate: 30 April 2027. Production requires security sign-off, executed BAA, and an issued PO. All three are open.

Other two shortlisted vendors held for re-evaluation if the pilot does not clear.

notes.title: Board IT Committee Update — March
notes.content:
Presented to the Board IT Committee, 4 March 2027.

Clinical documentation burden remains the top-cited driver of clinician dissatisfaction in the annual survey. A limited pilot is under way on two units to test whether AI-assisted documentation reduces after-hours charting time.

No production data is in scope. Results expected end of Q2.

Portfolio health: 94% of applications in supported versions, up from 89%.

notes.title: IT Application Inventory — summary
notes.content:
412 applications in the inventory.
- Production: term 318
- Pilot or limited use: 22
- Sunset scheduled: 41
- Unsupported version: 31 (down from 58 last year)

Owner assigned for 398 of 412. The 14 without an owner are all in the sunset list.

notes.title: Vendor Onboarding — process note
notes.content:
A vendor reaches production only after all four are complete:
1. Security assessment closed by the SOC, with any residual risk accepted by the CISO
2. Business-associate agreement executed, if PHI is in scope
3. Purchase order issued
4. Named application owner assigned in the inventory

Steps 1 and 2 are not mine to sign off. Vendors ask me to accelerate them; I cannot.

notes.title: Steering Committee — standing agenda
notes.content:
Monthly, first Tuesday, 09:00 ET.
Standing items: portfolio health, capital burn, open vendor reviews, incident summary, decision log.
Attendees: CIO, CISO, Privacy Officer, Clinical Informatics lead, Procurement, Contracts Counsel.

notes.title: Endpoint Refresh — status
notes.content: 1,100 devices in scope, 640 replaced. On track for June completion. 62 shared workstations on the pilot units are in the deferred group — they will be refreshed after the documentation pilot closes so we do not change two variables at once.

notes.title: Notes on the Lumen re-evaluation
notes.content: If the TechFlow pilot does not clear the April gate, the fallback is to re-open the category. Procurement holds the pricing detail from the original round; I do not, deliberately — the budget owner should not be anchored on a competitor's number while a live negotiation is running.

notes.title: Documentation pilot — decision gate, vendor-facing
notes.content:
Shared with TechFlow AI. Updated 12 March 2027.

Decision gate: 30 April 2027.

Production requires all three: security sign-off, executed BAA, issued purchase order. All three are currently open, and none of them is mine to grant.

Pilot scope is unchanged: two medical-surgical units, de-identified data only, per the Privacy Officer's determination.

This view carries scope and timing. It does not carry budget, sourcing, or evaluation detail.

notes.title: Network refresh — Site 4 commissioning
notes.content:
Core switches in, edge stack scheduled for the 18th. Fibre run through the east corridor came in under estimate for once.

Outstanding: the wireless survey has to be redone after the ceiling work, which nobody costed.

notes.title: Application rationalisation — FY27 targets
notes.content:
412 applications, target 360 by year end. 41 already flagged for sunset.

The hard part is not the sunsetting, it is the 14 with no assigned owner. Every one of them turns out to matter to somebody the moment you propose switching it off.

notes.title: Storage growth
notes.content:
Imaging archive growing 14% year on year, faster than the refresh cycle assumed. At this rate we buy again in eighteen months rather than thirty.

Worth modelling tiering before we just buy more.

notes.title: Disaster recovery test — annual
notes.content:
Ran the failover on 22 February. Recovery time objective met for tier 1, missed for tier 2 by about forty minutes.

The miss was DNS propagation, which is embarrassing and cheap to fix. Report went to the board committee with the miss stated plainly, which I would rather do than have it found.

notes.title: Helpdesk staffing model
notes.content:
Bea has been running the desk with one fewer than establishment since November. Ticket volumes are flat so the numbers do not show a problem, but first-response time has drifted eleven minutes.

That is a recruitment conversation and I have not had it.

notes.title: Printer fleet — the perennial
notes.content:
Fourteen models across four sites, six of them out of support. Consolidation proposal has been drafted twice and deferred twice.

Every IT department has this note and every one of them has deferred it.

notes.title: Board IT committee — standing membership
notes.content:
Chair rotates annually. Current: the finance non-exec. Meets quarterly, papers a week ahead.

They ask about cyber every single time, and the honest answer is always more nuanced than the slide.

notes.title: Interoperability programme — regional
notes.content:
Regional data-sharing initiative, three health systems. We are the smallest and therefore the one that has to do the most work to participate.

My position is that we join at phase two, not phase one. Being first here buys reputation and costs a year.

notes.title: Licence true-up
notes.content:
Annual reconciliation found us over-licensed on two products and under on one. Net position favourable but the under-licensed one is the awkward conversation.

Procurement is handling it. I do not want a surprise audit finding on this.

notes.title: Mobile device policy — refresh
notes.content:
Current policy predates the current device estate. Draft update circulated to the security and privacy leads.

Main change: personal devices accessing clinical applications require enrolment, which will be unpopular and is not negotiable.

notes.title: Weekly IT leadership — standing agenda
notes.content: Mondays 09:00. Incidents, projects, people, spend. Twenty minutes, and it overruns whenever anyone says the word 'quick'.

notes.title: Capital planning cycle — how it actually runs
notes.content:
Submissions in September, finance committee in November, approvals in December, spend from April.

Anything that arrives outside that window is competing against the contingency line, which is why mid-year requests are so hard.

notes.title: EHR upgrade — 2027 major release
notes.content: Vendor's annual release lands in October. Eight weeks of build and test, four weekends of clinical downtime rehearsal. It consumes the second half of the year and every other project plans around it.

notes.title: Telephony migration
notes.content: Moving off the legacy PBX. Ward phones are the hard part — nurses will not accept a headset and the handsets have to be cleanable.

notes.title: Application rationalisation
notes.content: 412 applications for 4,100 staff is too many. 41 are on the sunset list and 14 of those have no owner, which is why they are still running.

notes.title: Managed IT contract — Northgate, renewal
notes.content: Three-year term, renews January. Service is good, pricing is mid-market, and the scoping on privileged access is tight, which matters more than the rate.

notes.title: Clinical engineering — the boundary argument
notes.content: Medical devices sit with clinical engineering, not IT, and they are on the network. The segmentation programme needs both and reports to neither. This is a governance problem I have not solved in four years.

notes.title: IT service satisfaction survey
notes.content: 3.9 of 5, up from 3.6. Free-text comments are dominated by password resets and by not knowing who to call, which are the two things a service desk exists to fix.

notes.title: Interoperability mandate — regulatory
notes.content: New information-blocking requirements land next year. Compliance is mostly configuration but the attestation is mine to sign, which changes how carefully I want it done.

notes.title: Why I do not hold the security decision
notes.content: Asked regularly, usually by a vendor hoping for a shortcut. The CISO accepts risk because if the person who owns the budget also accepted the risk, the risk would always be accepted.

notes.title: Capital committee — how a line gets funded
notes.content: Business case, clinical sponsor, total cost over five years, and a named owner. Requests without a clinical sponsor do not make the agenda.

notes.title: Staff turnover in IT
notes.content: Two analysts left in six months, both to health systems paying twelve to fifteen per cent more. We are not going to win on rate, which means winning on scope of work or not at all.
